::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_21 — OrgPath and Federal AI Governance
:::


::: {.callout-note}
Federal agencies have inventoried more than 1,800 deployed and piloted AI systems under OMB M-25-21 — and almost none of those systems are governed at the identity layer. Service accounts with no owner, credentials that predate the system's ATO, AI agents acting inside Entra tenants with no OrgPath, no lifecycle process, and no ownership record: this is the hidden identity surface the federal AI expansion has created. This book shows how OrgPath's organizational-placement model governs the AI surface the same way it governs every other surface — by making the owning bureau, the authorization boundary, and the credential lifecycle deterministic rather than tribal.
:::

## Planned chapter outline

> This book is in draft. Chapters will be authored as individual `Book_21_CPT_NN.qmd` files.

| Chapter | Title | Spine arc |
|---------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | The Invisible Identity Surface | AD governed human identities; nobody built the equivalent for AI systems. The loss: 1,800+ federal AI deployments with unowned service accounts, no OrgPath, no lifecycle. |
| 2 | What M-25-21 Actually Requires | The OMB inventory mandate, the ATO requirement, and the high-impact governance checklist — and why those obligations are IAM obligations, not just reporting obligations. |
| 3 | Every AI System Is an Identity Subject | How the OMB inventory fields map to UIAO's machine-identity record: owning bureau → OrgPath, system_name_ato → credential anchor, vendor → non-employee surface, have_ato → ATO reciprocity. |
| 4 | Agentic AI — The Highest-Risk Machine Identity | Classification matters: an NLP classifier and an agentic AI system that submits forms, queries HR data, and triggers workflows are governed at different rungs of the L0–L4 actuation ladder. What makes agentic AI the highest-blast-radius machine identity class. |
| 5 | The ATO Gap — Deployed Without Authorization | One in N deployed AI systems has no ATO. How UIAO detects that gap: the DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ato-gap finding class, how it surfaces, and what a gated remediation loop looks like. |
| 6 | Shadow AI — Deployed Without Inventory | The worst case: an agentic AI system operating inside the Entra tenant that was never reported to OMB. How UIAO's machine-identity scan finds it, and what the governance disposition options are. |
| 7 | OrgPath as the Authorization Spine for AI | The same organizational position that governs PAM (Book_20) governs the AI surface: which systems a bureau is permitted to deploy, which credential tier they operate under, and which OrgPath node owns the blast radius if the system misbehaves. |
| 8 | The Machine-Identity Lifecycle for Federal AI | Joiner/mover/leaver for AI systems: provisioning at ATO, rotation on re-authorization, decommission on retirement. How the sailpoint-machine-identity adapter and the OMB inventory vintage cycle drive it. |
